neighbours.label: problem noun that is the object of a remedying verb (fill the vacancy, correct the distortion, repair the damage)
fire: The council hired extra staff to fill the gap left by the retirements.
Engineers added a filter to reduce the noise picked up by the cable.
The cream helps repair the damage done by years of sunbathing.
The bank cut interest rates to offset the slowdown in exports.
Glasses with special lenses correct the blurring caused by astigmatism.
The governor called an election to fill the seat left empty by the senator's death.
Ice packs reduce the swelling that follows a sprained ankle.
Software patches fix the vulnerabilities exploited by the attackers.
quiet: The council hired extra staff to run the library opened last spring.
Engineers added a filter to the cable before the concert started.
The cream smells of lavender and is sold in small blue jars.
The bank raised interest rates after a strong year for exports.
Glasses with thin frames are popular among students this year.
The governor called an election and the senator agreed to stand again.
Ice packs are kept in the freezer next to the frozen peas.
Software updates add new features requested by the users.

notes: Probe: 'fill the vacancy' 0.71, 'corrects the distortion' 0.61, 'protects the skin from damage' 0.58, 'Ear infections are' 0.22, 'struggled with a shortage' 0.11; neutral 'supply' 0.03, 'glow' 0.10, 'budget' 0.01. The remedy-verb frame looks stronger than the problem noun alone.
